name: Ranger 6
intro: Ranger 6 was a camera spacecraft built to dive straight into the Moon, taking pictures until the very end. It flew perfectly and hit its target in the Sea of Tranquility, but its cameras never turned on. All that’s left is a small crater and scattered scraps.
whyLeft: Rangers had no brakes or legs: hitting the Moon was always the plan. Ranger 6 just did it without sending a single picture.
repurpose: There is nothing left to fix, but its crater is a time marker: scientists can compare it with nearby natural craters to see how fast fresh scars fade.
funFact: Five years after Ranger 6 crashed, Apollo 11 landed in the same Sea of Tranquility.

hotspots.title: Impact crater
hotspots.text: Ranger 6 slammed in here faster than a rifle bullet. The spacecraft was smashed to pieces and left a small, fresh crater.

hotspots.title: Dead cameras
hotspots.text: Investigators worked out what went wrong: about two minutes after launch, the TV system switched on by accident for 67 seconds and an electrical spark, called an arc, most likely fried it. The cameras were dead long before the Moon.

photo.alt: The Ranger TV camera system with six cameras
photo.caption: The six-camera TV system used on Rangers 6 to 9. Ranger 6’s set never sent a picture.

hotspots.title: Scattered scraps
hotspots.text: Scout, scan the ground around the crater. Any pieces left are small, twisted bits of metal mixed into the soil. There is nothing here to repair.

hotspots.title: Perfect aim
hotspots.text: Everything else worked: Ranger 6 flew 65.5 hours and hit right on target, nose pointed the right way. That good aim gave engineers hope, and six months later Ranger 7 succeeded.
